linkedin:
Compile with `go build -o app` and you get one self-contained binary, no runtime to install.

Put it on a managed Linux server and run it under **systemd** so it stays up and restarts on reboot. Read the port from `os.Getenv("PORT")`, put a reverse proxy in front for your domain and SSL, and run a managed Postgres or MySQL alongside. This is the server-based path, not a one-click Go runtime, and Go doesn't need one.

Read the full guide: https://www.kloudbean.com/blog/deploy-golang-app/

Deploying a Go App Is Almost Boring (Here's Why)

Quick thread 🧵
Compile with `go build -o app` and you get one self-contained binary, no runtime to install.
Put it on a managed Linux server and run it under **systemd** so it stays up and restarts on reboot.
Read the port from `os.Getenv("PORT")`, put a reverse proxy in front for your domain and SSL, and run a managed Postgres or MySQL alongside.
This is the server-based path, not a one-click Go runtime, and Go doesn't need one.
